title.narrative: IOM Migration och utveckling i Latinamerika
IOM Regional Migration and Development Latinamerica

description.narrative: Stöd till IOM för ett projekt som, under 2022 och 2023 och på regional nivå, bidrar till att venezuelanska migranter blir bättre integrerade socialt och ekonomiskt i sina värdsamhällen. Projektet inkluderar stöd till reglerad migration som ger uppehålls-och arbetstillstånd, utveckling av de offentliga arbetsförmedlingarna, insatser för att underlätta migranters egenföretagande, stöd till lokala myndigheters arbete med lokal integrering och till civilsamhället för att främja migranters deltagande i beslut som rör integration.

Support to IOM for a project that will, during 2022 and 2023 and at regional level, contribute to Venezuelan migrants being better integrated socially and economically in their host communities. The project include support to the regularization process, support to the public employment agencies to extend their services to migrants, strengthen the entrepreneurial skills of migrants, support to local authorise to design and carry out integration activities in a participatory manner and strengthen the capacity of civil society to enable broader participation of migrants in decision making.

The overall objective of the project is to contribute, at a regional level, to Venezuelan migrants being better integrated socially and economically in their host communities.
This objective should be achieved through two main outcomes:
1. Migrants are able to generate income as a result of integrated and harmonized regularization processes; improved access to employment opportunities; and capacities to start their own businesses.
2. Migrant integration needs, challenges and priorities are reflected in local, national and regional policies and decision-making bodies/forums and efficiently and appropriately addressed by local actors.

sector.narrative: Facilitation of orderly, safe, regular and responsible migration and mobility

description.narrative:
The final report and the evaluation conclude that the project contributed to increased levels of migrant integration, in particular, social integration.
Examples of results related to Outcome 1: Migrants are able to generate income as a result of integrated and harmonized regularization processes; improved access to employment opportunities; and capacities to start their own businesses.
The project published a total of 5 studies on migrant contributions to economic development (in Panama, Dominican Republic, Aruba, Chile, and Costa Rica), as well as 3 regional thematic studies relevant to integration (regularization; migrants in situations of vulnerability; private sector role in integration). Results from these studies were presented to national stakeholders as well as in various regional fora (R4V, Quito Process, Migrant Women Leaders Network, CAVEX), and reported in various national and international media outlets. The primary impact was the use of these studies for advocacy purposes, in particular with government counterparts, to change perceptions and policies regarding migrants. A concrete result is that the passage of a labour law that would have been detrimental to migrant economic integration in Panama was blocked due to advocacy efforts from the Regional Network of Venezuelan Chambers of Commerce (CAVEX), who used data from a study on migrant contributions, published with support from the project.
155 migrants and members of the host community (35% women; 65% men) were provided with support to access employment opportunities. More specifically, 34 migrants in Panama were provided with legal support to regularize their migratory status and obtain work permits. These migrants also received support in soft skills training and to register with the Ministry of Labours job bank. In Brazil, 121 migrants and members of the host community were provided with vocational and soft skills training and job placement to work in the rapidly growing renewable energy sector as installers of photovoltaic solar panels.
316 migrants and host community members were provided with entrepreneurial support. More specifically, within one month of its launch, 97 persons (81% women; 19% men) across 15 countries accessed the online training on Migrant Entrepreneurship that was developed under the project, in collaboration with UN Women and ILO. In addition, 219 Venezuelan micro-, small- and medium- sized entrepreneurs (69% women; 31% men) were provided with support to access national and regional trade fairs and negotiation rounds. This enabled them to generate a total of USD 57,000 in additional income as well as a total of USD 240,000 worth of sales quotes and trade agreements. As their businesses expanded, they were also able to create 21 new employment opportunities for both migrants and host communities. To ensure these migrant entrepreneurs are provided with the necessary support, the project also contributed to the establishment of the Venezuelan Chambers of Commerce in Argentina and Uruguay and supported the Regional Network of Venezuelan Chambers of Commerce (CAVEX), e.g. the development of the website.
Examples of results related to Outcome 2: Migrant integration needs, challenges and priorities are reflected in local, national and regional policies and decision-making bodies/forums and efficiently and appropriately addressed by local actors.
Twelve national governments are better informed and coordinated to support migrant integration. More specifically, IOM as technical secretariate financed through the project, supported the Presidency Pro Tempore of the Quito Process to carry out 12 face-to-face meetings, 45 webinars, and organized the Quito Process Plenary in 2022 and 2023. The project was also instrumental in achieving, for the first time, participation of the Venezuelan CSOs through Coalition for Venezuela and the private sector through CAVEX in the Quito Process. Both the Coalition for Venezuela and CAVEX have received capacity strengthening support through the project. Among the main results of the Quito Process during the project period were strengthening of the Group of Friends of the Quito Process, advances in the Integration Strategy and inclusion of work with host communities in the agenda.
Twelve municipalities in nine countries (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, Uruguay) have strengthened participatory processes and contributed to furthering migrant integration. More specifically, 27 local authorities were trained on community-based planning, after which, 12 community projects were implemented, based on community consultations. Decision makers and stakeholders are also better informed on needs and best practices faced by local authorities in the region in regard to migrant integration, as a result of the publication of a joint study with the Organization of American States (OAS), the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and the Pan-American Development Fund (PADF), which was launched at the Cities Summit of the Americas.
594 Civil Society Organizations (CSO) representatives in 17 countries increased capacities to deliver migrant integration support. More specifically, 311 CSO representatives from 14 countries participated in two online trainings to build their capacities in designing and implementing integration programs, in collaboration with the Latin American Faculty of Social Sciences (FLACSO). A training manual was also developed and published. In addition, 20 NGOs in 10 countries received in-kind support to strengthen their capacities to deliver integration support. In kind support to NGOs in Uruguay, Brazil and Peru were co-funded by Italy.
After a capacity development activity organized by the project in 2022 a Regional Network of Venezuelan Diaspora Women Leaders was created by 27 Venezuelan women diaspora leaders from 11 countries. The project organized and supported two regional in-person meetings and six virtual meetings for the network, all aimed to strengthen the capacities of these women diaspora leaders. The network has also independently generated activities in different countries, both exchange of experiences and coordination of assistance to migrants.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
